The supplied results do include a Zhou paper on wind-related bridge forecasting: Feiyu Zhou and Marios Impraimakis propose a transformer self-attention encoder-decoder for forecasting wind-induced structural response time series and supporting a digital twin for bridge structural health monitoring [1]. It is tested on real-world measurements from the Hardanger Bridge, compares predicted and measured vibrations to detect large deviations, and is positioned as an early-warning tool for structural change under changing environmental or traffic conditions [1].

If you meant wind power forecasting rather than bridge response forecasting, the other papers focus on wind energy, weather, or nowcasting rather than bridges [2,5,6,8,9]. So the direct match for “Zhou wind bridge forecasting” is the bridge structural response forecasting paper by Feiyu Zhou [1].
